en: I perpetually remember the daughter of Mātaṅga, composed by the great poet Śrī Kālidāsa in the Śyāmalā-daṇḍaka meter— she who makes even the jeweled lute of Māṇikya seem dull, whose playful speech is charming, and whose limbs are as delicate as sapphires, languid with passion.
Victory to you, daughter of Mātaṅga! Victory to you, who possess the luster of a blue lotus!
Victory to you, who delight in music! Victory to you, who are fond of your pet parrot!

Victory to you, O Mother! You who dwell within the forest of *bilva* trees growing on a jewel-island rising from the midst of the ocean of nectar; you who delight in residing in the celestial *kadamba* grove at the edge of the Kalpa; you who are dear to the wearer of the tiger-skin (Śiva) and beloved by all the worlds!

You whose three eyes are graced by locks of hair bound with *nīpa* garlands, trembling in the flurry of reverence for the musical performances commenced with devotion; you, the daughter of the Mountain!
You who are adorned by a mass of very glossy dark-blue curls bound by the rays of the streaks of yellow silk that serve as your crest-ornament; you who are honored by the world!

I delight in her, who is as intoxicating as the gods; whose eyes create the illusion of being a cluster of flowers upon the creeper-like brows resembling the bow of Kāmalīlā, and which are sprinkled with the nectar of speech; who is enchanting with the playful beauty of lovely gorocanā paste;

whose cheeks, radiant with a circle of moonlight from a string of shimmering young pearls, are adorned with musk-leaf patterns whose fragrance bewilders female bees, whose humming intensifies the deep resonance of the lute strings.

O you of beautiful voice and radiant splendor; O you adorned with exquisite ornaments of earrings fashioned from trembling *tālī* leaves as if for the practice of playing the lute, honored by the *siddhas*;

O you whose single blue lotus on one ear is captivated by the beauty of the swaying glance of eyes languid with the intoxication of divine wine; O you who are the auspicious fruit that fulfills the desires of all the worlds without exception!

O Kālī, whose nostril-pendants of pearl cast doubt upon the mass of flowing beauty from drops of perspiration shimmering on Your forehead; You who are the soul of the entire universe; You whose face is radiant with a charming, gentle smile and a cluster of betel-nuts, camphor, and spices; You who hold the gesture of wisdom (jñānamudrā) and bestow all prosperity; You whose hand holds a lotus that shines like the sun;

You whose red lips smile through the union of the stainless luster of Your rows of teeth, which are as smooth as jasmine flowers; You who hold a beautiful lute and possess lips like the ripe *bimba* fruit. // 1 //
O Mantharā, abode of the fine arts, whose neck bears the graceful charm of a conch emerging from the overflowing milk-ocean of beauty at the rise of the moon of her exquisite new youth;
O auspicious one, resplendent with the flawless radiance of the moon, illuminated by necklaces and other ornaments veiled by the lovely luster of divine gems;
O you who are honored by yogis, adorned with creeper-like arms shimmering with the sprout-like clusters of rays from jeweled armlets!
To her whose hands are adorned with bracelets shimmering with the ruby-like luster pervading the entire circle of the quarters; who is graced by playful charm and honored by practitioners;

whose pair of hands rivals the lotuses blooming at the break of day; who is non-dual and possesses ever-rising compassion; whose sprout-like fingers appear like twilight due to the mass of light from divine jewel rings, and upon which the orb of moonlight from her nails shines forth; she before whom Indra bows, and whose circle of consciousness radiates with glittering earrings.

To her who is a mine of jewels of form and beauty, revealed by the surging waves of the folds of skin on her creeper-like waist as it bows under the weight of her lovely breasts—smiling with necklaces resembling clusters of stars; she whose hands hold a lute and bring glory to her servants; she who is bent by the burden of her high, golden-pitcher-like breasts and who bows over the three worlds; she who is adorned with a line of dark hair that creates the illusion of moss upon the shore of the lake of her shining, round, and deep navel; she whose speech is sweet.
In that place, where the tinkling of beautiful waist-bands mocked the twang of the bowstring of the God of Love; where celestial garments of jewels were worn;
where the surface of the golden earth was surpassed by the splendor of her hips, radiant with a girdle shimmering like rubies; and which was as cool as moonlight—(2).

O Goddess of dark luster, whose thighs possess a beautiful splendor covered by divine garments as red as blooming fresh *kiṃśuka* flowers, surpassing the reddish hue of the trunk-iron-bar of Indra’s elephant; O You of unrestrained majesty, whose noble creeper-like calves evoke the suspicion that they are quivers for the God of Love made of smooth, tender blue sapphire;

O You of graceful, playful gait, who shine with the brilliance of moon-like nails sparkling in the company of deer that mistake them for sprouts of *dūrvā* grass produced by the mass of smooth, dark radiance from the hair of the wives of the bowing world-protectors; O Radiant One, O Immaculate One!

O Umā, whose lotus feet are the abode of the beauty of youth, reddened by the intense lac-dye of the morning sunlight as it rubs against the crest-jewels of millions of gods, lords of wealth, lords of spirits, lords of waters, lords of speech, lords of death, lords of demons, lords of yakṣas, wind-gods, and fire-gods—O you of beautiful feet! 3.
Seated upon a beautiful and excellent jewel-throne,
well-established on a jeweled lotus-seat and a jeweled lion-throne, supported by two conch-shells and lotuses,
and accompanied there by Vighneśa, Durgā, Baṭuka, and Kṣetrapāla.

O Goddess, who are accompanied by a multitude of intoxicated young female elephants; who are honored by beautiful women such as Menakā and others; who are surrounded by the eight Bhairavas; who are served by the Śaktis beginning with Vāmā;
and who are joined by the eight Śaktis beginning with Dhātrī and Lakṣmī.
Adorned with the maṇḍalas of the Mātṛkās,
honored by the maṇḍalas of yakṣas, gandharvas, and siddha-maidens,
you whose nature consists of the five arrows.
When you were not attended by Rati with the five-arrowed god [Kāma],
and when you were gladdened by Vasanta who partakes in joy,
you were fit for the highest welfare as one who possesses devotion.
You shine in the minds of yogis; you blaze with the power of the Vedic meters;
you are fully honored by Kṛṣṇa, who is insatiably devoted to the pleasure of the art of song.
You are praised by the Creator with a devoted mind;
you are sung by the Vidyādharas with music that is pleasing to all hearts. // 4 //
You are sung of by the *kiṃnaras* with lutes whose sweet sounds are skilled at captivating the ear;
you are worshipped by circles of *yakṣa*, *gandharva*, and *siddha* maidens;
and you are propitiated by the wives of the gods, who long for every form of auspicious fortune.

You sport, fondling that parrot which embodies the excellence of all branches of knowledge; its throat-root throbs with three rows of shimmering colors, its two wings are soft, dark, and magnificent, and its beak’s splendor far surpasses the *kiṃśuka* flower. Holding a crystal rosary, a book whose essence is the nectar of wisdom, and a goad and a noose with your two lotus-hands, the Goddess of Speech—in the form of prose and verse—emerges from the mouth of one by whom you are thus meditated upon.
One should emerge [from meditation].
Or, by whichever form one meditates—whether as one who subsists on barley or as one possessing the luster of refined gold—the women and men become subject to that person's will;
or, he who meditates with the radiance of refined gold sports amidst thousands of goddesses of fortune.
What could not be accomplished for one who meditates upon your dark and tender form, adorned with the moon upon its crest?
For him, the ocean is a pleasure-lake; sandalwood is his pleasure-grove; the earth is his auspicious throne; the Goddess of Speech is his servant, and Śrī herself is his obedient handmaid.
O you who are the essence of all holy places, the essence of all mantras, the essence of all tantras, the essence of all yantras, and the essence of all powers!

O you who are the essence of all seats, the essence of all principles, the essence of all vidyās, the essence of all yogas, the essence of all nādas, the essence of all sounds, the essence of the entire universe, the essence of all initiations, the essence of all that exists; O omnipresent one, protect me, protect me, protect me!
O Goddess, homage to you! O Goddess, homage to you! O Goddess, homage to you! // 5 //
May the auspicious Mātaṅgī, dark as an emerald, full of passion,
and dwelling in the Kadamba forest, cast her sidelong glances upon me.
Thus ends the Śyāmalā-daṇḍaka composed by the great poet, the illustrious Kālidāsa.
